lines.trans: Vika, forgive me once again.
Are you still here?
I have not talked to her yet.
I am warning you: step back!
Chef, why did you not turn back?
I always used to do that.
Now the time has come to answer for my actions.
Before you and our daughter!
Vika, do whatever you want, I will still be right beside you.
Because I love you both.
There is a chance that everything will work out!
Hang on, chef, we will pull you out right now!

lines.trans: I will always be right beside you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Будущую? Я ещё не в таком статусе.
examples.trans: Future? I am not in that status yet.

examples.text: Утро, а ты ещё не отмечаешь?
examples.trans: It is morning, and you are not celebrating yet?
Understood. We will think some more.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты забыла? У вас послезавтра развод!
examples.trans: Did you forget? Your divorce is the day after tomorrow!

examples.text: Всё, что мне от тебя нужно, — это завтрашний развод!
examples.trans: All that I need from you is tomorrow's divorce!
Excuse me, I will sort it out.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.text: Простите, я вас не заметила. Вы мне нос сломали!
examples.trans: Forgive me, I did not notice you. You broke my nose!
Vika, forgive me once again.

examples.text: Знаешь что, давай ты лучше дома переночуешь.

examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сегодня он ей подарок сделает, завтра она его в бар отпустит.
examples.trans: Today he will give her a gift, tomorrow she will let him go to the bar.

examples.text: Егор, слушай, Виктория Сергеевна попросила отнести это вино в номер, который она сняла.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you. Sorry that I bothered you.
Alright, good night.
And in the meantime have some coffee.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, do not stay silent.
Can you bring me something?
Yes, of course!

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Я с ней ещё пока не поговорил.
examples.trans: I have not talked to her yet.
Talk to him.
We need to talk.

meanings.en: to warn, to give advance notice
meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упреждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'warn', paired with 'предупредить'.

examples.trans: I am warning you: step back!
I warned you.
I am warning you for the last time.

meanings.en: to step aside, to move back
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'step aside', paired with 'отходить'.

examples.trans: I am warning you: step back!
Step back from the car!
He stepped over to the window.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.text: Ну, скажите мне, почему вместо кулона появилось кольцо?
examples.trans: Well, tell me, why did a ring appear instead of a pendant?

Why are we going so slowly?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'returned, turned back', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.text: Я всегда верил, что вы с Виктором Петровичем поженитесь.
examples.trans: I always believed that you and Viktor Petrovich would get married.

meanings.en: to work out, sort itself out; to form
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'разоваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to work out, form', paired with 'образовываться'.

examples.trans: Everything will still work out.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'stick (with)'.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё будет хорошо.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').
